_readme: Allowlist for tools/check-backlog-citations.mjs. Every key is a (BL|BUG|DEBT)-N id cited somewhere in tracked source that does NOT resolve via `backlog get-item --repo sox-ecosystem --human-id <id>`. Each entry's `reason` records WHY that's expected/acceptable rather than a defect, so this file stays a legible audit trail and not a growing pile of silenced red. Compiled 2026-08-18 remediating DEBT-006. `cause` is one of: PLAN_LOCAL_BUG014 (docs/plan/bug014-store-hardening/SPEC.md T1-T11 own numbering colliding with the graph's BUG/DEBT families), PLAN_LOCAL_RUNTIME_PROD (a SECOND, independently-discovered collision: docs/plan/runtime-productionization/ has its own BL-1xx work-package numbering that collides with the graph's real BL family — NOT part of DEBT-006's original diagnosis, found during this remediation, not yet disambiguated at the source because that plan is outside this packet's scope), MIGRATION_DROPPED (existed as a real heading in BACKLOG.md history pre-2026-08-06 migration, never carried into the graph), STILL_LOST (existed briefly during the 2026-08-14 backlog data-loss incident, explicitly recorded in HANDOFF-20260814.md §C as unrecoverable from any transcript), NOT_A_CITATION (the regex matched prose/example/fixture content that was never intended as a real backlog reference), or SUPERSEDED_BY_NEW_FILING (this remediation filed a real graph item for the underlying work; a residual bare mention of the old placeholder id remains in a historical narrative string).

BUG-022.reason: HANDOFF-20260814.md §C, explicit: 'Still lost, not refilable from session record — these are recovery targets: the first sweep's epics (formerly DEBT-008…014, BUG-022), BUG-029...'. Verified zero matches searching the current graph for any content resembling this destroyed item. ID REUSE (2026-08-18): the graph has since allocated BUG-022 to a brand-new, unrelated item ('idle-flush ungated strategy self-perpetuates: _performIdleFlush's executeGet re-arms the timer forever'). The HANDOFF reference is a historical record of what was destroyed and must keep the original string, disambiguated inline there via the id-reuse table. The store-adapter citations (turso-adapter.ts:605, idle-flush-adaptive.bl590.sqlite.spec.ts, idle-flush-ungated-self-rearm.bug022.spec.ts) were verified 2026-08-19 via `backlog get-item --human-id BUG-022` to genuinely mean the NEW item, not the lost epic — they describe the exact same ungated-self-rearm mechanism the graph item's body does, and two of the three now carry inline prose making that explicit. Left as-is — see disambiguatedRefs.

SPEC.md's PLAN-LOCAL IDS banner (rewritten 2026-08-19 for this remediation) also names DEBT-008 explicitly while describing the id-reuse mechanism itself — both are disambiguated inline, not by accident — see disambiguatedRefs.

BL-320.reason: Confirmed present and substantively discussed (not just a passing mention) throughout BACKLOG.md at commit e547e93b^ — memory-core's JSONL telemetry sink (libs/memory-core/src/telemetry.ts), described as 'already writes JSONL... live right now'. This is the item DEBT-006's own citation [5] points at. NOT bulk-imported: BL-353 ('Telemetry is written to disk and never read: 75k events, two days, zero analysis') in the CURRENT graph appears to be the direct successor/supersession of this exact concern — re-filing BL-320 fresh would likely duplicate BL-353. Recommend the repo owner decide whether to (a) leave as superseded-by-BL-353 and allowlist permanently, or (b) file a thin BL-320 stub purely so historical citations resolve, cross-linked to BL-353. Left as (a) allowlisted pending that decision — see DEBT-006 remediation notes.
